<!-- Generated by tools/docgen from doc comments. Do not edit: run scripts/docs.sh. -->

```odin
import record "fire:record"
```

Recording: audio takes written to disk, MIDI and automation recorded into
clips, and loop recording, all placed on a timeline.

- An `Audio_Recorder` is a graph node: connect any signal to its inputs
  (the device input, a bus, a track to resample). While armed and its
  timeline plays, it copies what arrives into blocks that a
  `Disk_Writer` thread writes as WAV takes. Finished takes come back from
  `audio_recorder_poll` with their timeline position, ready to become
  audio clips.
- A `Midi_Recorder` records the events it receives into MIDI clips, one
  per take; `midi_recorder_progress` shows the take so far, for
  overdubbing as you play.
- An `Automation_Recorder` passes the app's control moves on to a node
  and writes them into automation (touch or latch); merge the ranges into
  a lane with `clip.automation_merge`.
- **Latency.** A performer plays along with output they hear late, and
  their signal reaches the recorder later again. Recorders shift what
  they record by `latency_frames`, the round trip: use
  `backend.round_trip_latency_frames` once the device runs, or measure it
  with a `Latency_Probe` and a loopback cable.
- **Punch in and out** limit recording to a range of the timeline.
- **Loop recording.** When the timeline wraps while recording, the take
  ends and the next pass starts a new one, so every pass is kept.

```odin
disk, _ := record.disk_writer_create({})
defer record.disk_writer_destroy(disk)
node, rec, _ := record.audio_recorder_create(disk, {timeline = song, channels = 2, directory = "takes", name = "vocal"})
id, _ := graph.add_node(g, node, 2, 0)
graph.connect(g, graph.INPUT, 0, id, 0)
graph.connect(g, graph.INPUT, 1, id, 1)
graph.commit(g)
// once the device runs:
record.audio_recorder_set_latency(rec, backend.round_trip_latency_frames(&dev))
record.audio_recorder_arm(rec, true)
// ... play the song; then, regularly:
for take in record.audio_recorder_poll(rec) do use(take) // a clip of take.path, placed at take.start
```

See /guides/recording/ for more.

## Constants

### BLOCK_FRAMES

```odin
BLOCK_FRAMES :: 4096
```

Frames per block handed from the audio thread to the disk.

### MAX_CHANNELS

```odin
MAX_CHANNELS :: 64
```

Most channels a take may have.

### AUDIO_RECORDER_TYPE_ID

```odin
AUDIO_RECORDER_TYPE_ID :: "fire.audio_recorder"
```

Saved-state ID of `audio_recorder_create` nodes (settings only: takes and
arming are not saved).

### MIDI_RECORDER_TYPE_ID

```odin
MIDI_RECORDER_TYPE_ID :: "fire.midi_recorder"
```

Saved-state ID of `midi_recorder_create` nodes (settings only).

### AUTOMATION_RECORDER_TYPE_ID

```odin
AUTOMATION_RECORDER_TYPE_ID :: "fire.automation_recorder"
```

Saved-state ID of `automation_recorder_create` nodes (settings only).

### LATENCY_PROBE_TYPE_ID

```odin
LATENCY_PROBE_TYPE_ID :: "fire.latency_probe"
```

Saved-state ID of `latency_probe_create` nodes.

## Types

### Audio_Recorder_Settings

```odin
Audio_Recorder_Settings :: struct {
	timeline: core.Timeline_Id,
	channels: int,
	directory: string,
	name: string,
	encoding: audiofile.Sample_Format,
	latency_frames: int,
	buffer_seconds: f64,
}
```

Settings for `audio_recorder_create`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `timeline` | takes are placed on it and recorded while it plays; zero = record whenever armed |
| `channels` | the node's inputs, and the takes' channels |
| `directory` | where take files go (must exist) |
| `name` | take files are `<directory>/<name>-<n>.wav`, n counting from 1 |
| `encoding` | of the files: .Int16, .Int24, .Int32 or .Float32 (the zero value, .Int8, means .Float32) |
| `latency_frames` | round trip to compensate: see the package doc |
| `buffer_seconds` | audio held for the disk at 48 kHz; 0 = 4 s |

### Take

```odin
Take :: struct {
	path: string,
	run: int,
	pass: int,
	start: timebase.Beats,
	length: timebase.Beats,
	start_frame: i64,
	frames: i64,
	sample_rate: f64,
	channels: int,
	dropped_frames: i64,
	error: audiofile.Error,
}
```

A finished take: a file and where it belongs. Free its path with
`take_destroy`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `path` | the WAV file |
| `run` | counts recordings: a new run starts at each start, punch-in or locate |
| `pass` | loop passes within the run, from 0 |
| `start` | timeline position of the first frame |
| `length` | timeline beats the take covers |
| `start_frame` | clock frame (after latency compensation) of the first frame |
| `frames` |  |
| `sample_rate` |  |
| `channels` |  |
| `dropped_frames` | written as silence because the disk fell behind |
| `error` | the file could not be written (then `frames` is what was) |

### Audio_Recorder

```odin
Audio_Recorder :: struct {...}
```

Records its inputs to disk as takes. From `audio_recorder_create`; the
node owns it and frees it when destroyed. Procs not marked [rt] are for
the control thread. Fields are internal.

### Write_Mode

```odin
Write_Mode :: enum u8 {
	Touch,
	Latch,
}
```

What happens when the user lets go of a control that was being written.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Touch` | writing stops on release |
| `Latch` | writing goes on with the last value until the take ends (a stop, a disarm, a punch-out, a loop wrap) |

### Automation_Recorder_Settings

```odin
Automation_Recorder_Settings :: struct {
	timeline: core.Timeline_Id,
	mode: Write_Mode,
	max_params: int,
	max_events: int,
	glide_ms: f64,
}
```

Settings for `automation_recorder_create`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `timeline` | positions are taken from it, and it records while it plays |
| `mode` |  |
| `max_params` | parameters written at once; 0 = 64 |
| `max_events` | changes held for the control thread; 0 = 8192 (more are dropped and counted) |
| `glide_ms` | a move is written as the old value held, then this glide to the new one (as the node's smoothing heard it); 0 = 10 ms, negative = jumps |

### Automation_Take

```odin
Automation_Take :: struct {
	param: core.Param_Id,
	run: int,
	pass: int,
	start: timebase.Beats,
	end: timebase.Beats,
	points: []clip.Automation_Point,
}
```

A range of one parameter's curve as the user drew it. Merge it into a
lane with `clip.automation_merge`; free `points` with `delete`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `param` |  |
| `run` | counts recordings: a new run starts at each start, punch-in or locate |
| `pass` | loop passes within the run, from 0 |
| `start` | timeline positions written over |
| `end` |  |
| `points` | linear points at timeline positions, from `start` to `end`: each value held until the next move, then a glide to it |

### Automation_Recorder

```odin
Automation_Recorder :: struct {...}
```

Moves parameters for the user and records the moves. The app sends a
control's values through it instead of `graph.set_param`; it passes them
to the node it is event-connected to, at the start of its next block,
and while armed and playing records them into takes. From
`automation_recorder_create`; the node owns it and frees it when
destroyed. Procs not marked [rt] are for the control thread, which must
call `automation_recorder_poll` regularly. Fields are internal.

### Latency_Probe_Settings

```odin
Latency_Probe_Settings :: struct {
	max_seconds: f64,
	burst_frames: int,
	level: f32,
}
```

Settings for `latency_probe_create`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `max_seconds` | longest round trip to look for; 0 = 1 s |
| `burst_frames` | length of the noise burst played; 0 = 4096 |
| `level` | the burst's peak level, linear; 0 = 0.25 (−12 dBFS) |

### Latency_Probe

```odin
Latency_Probe :: struct {...}
```

Measures the round trip a recorder must compensate: plays a noise burst
on its output and finds it in its input. Connect its output to the
device output and its input from the device input, with a loopback cable
between them (or a microphone near a speaker), and keep it in the graph
where the recorders are. From `latency_probe_create`; the node owns it.
Fields are internal.

### Midi_Recorder_Settings

```odin
Midi_Recorder_Settings :: struct {
	timeline: core.Timeline_Id,
	latency_frames: int,
	max_events: int,
}
```

Settings for `midi_recorder_create`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `timeline` | takes are placed on it and recorded while it plays; zero = record whenever armed |
| `latency_frames` | how late events arrive after they were played (usually 0 for MIDI) |
| `max_events` | events held for the control thread; 0 = 8192 (more are dropped and counted) |

### Midi_Take

```odin
Midi_Take :: struct {
	clip: ^clip.Midi_Clip,
	run: int,
	pass: int,
	start: timebase.Beats,
	length: timebase.Beats,
}
```

A finished MIDI take: a clip of what was played, from `start` on the
timeline. Release the clip with `clip.midi_clip_release`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `clip` | notes from the take's start; `length` beats long |
| `run` | counts recordings: a new run starts at each start, punch-in or locate |
| `pass` | loop passes within the run, from 0 |
| `start` | timeline position of the clip's beat 0 |
| `length` |  |

### Midi_Recorder

```odin
Midi_Recorder :: struct {...}
```

Records the events it receives (notes, per-note expression, MIDI channel
messages) into clips. From `midi_recorder_create`; the node owns it and
frees it when destroyed. Procs not marked [rt] are for the control
thread, which must call `midi_recorder_poll` regularly (every UI frame,
say): that is where events become clips. Fields are internal.

### Disk_Writer_Settings

```odin
Disk_Writer_Settings :: struct {
	manual: bool,
}
```

Settings for `disk_writer_create`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `manual` | No thread: the app calls `disk_writer_service` to write, for example once per block in an offline render, so nothing is ever dropped. |

### Disk_Writer

```odin
Disk_Writer :: struct {...}
```

Writes the takes of any number of audio recorders on one background
thread. Control thread only. Fields are internal.

## Procedures

### audio_recorder_create

```odin
audio_recorder_create :: proc(disk: ^Disk_Writer, settings: Audio_Recorder_Settings, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (node: core.Node, r: ^Audio_Recorder, err: core.Error)
```

Control thread. Makes a recorder node with `settings.channels` inputs and
no outputs, served by `disk`. `.Invalid_Argument` without channels, a
directory or a name.

### audio_recorder_arm

```odin
audio_recorder_arm :: proc(r: ^Audio_Recorder, armed: bool) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Arms or disarms the recorder, from its next block. Armed,
it records while its timeline plays (and inside the punch range, if set).

### audio_recorder_set_latency

```odin
audio_recorder_set_latency :: proc(r: ^Audio_Recorder, frames: int) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Changes `latency_frames`, from the next block: set it
once the device runs, from `backend.round_trip_latency_frames`. Not while
recording.

### audio_recorder_set_punch

```odin
audio_recorder_set_punch :: proc(r: ^Audio_Recorder, punch_in: timebase.Beats, punch_out: timebase.Beats) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Records only from timeline position `punch_in` to
`punch_out` (after latency compensation).

### audio_recorder_clear_punch

```odin
audio_recorder_clear_punch :: proc(r: ^Audio_Recorder) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Removes the punch range.

### audio_recorder_poll

```odin
audio_recorder_poll :: proc(r: ^Audio_Recorder) -> (take: Take, ok: bool)
```

Control thread. The next finished take, if any (iterate with `for take in`).
The caller owns it: free with `take_destroy`.

### audio_recorder_status

```odin
audio_recorder_status :: proc "contextless"(r: ^Audio_Recorder) -> (recording: bool, dropped_frames: u64)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Whether a take is being recorded, and the frames lost so far because
the disk fell behind (written as silence).

### take_destroy

```odin
take_destroy :: proc(t: ^Take, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Frees a take's path (the file stays).

### automation_recorder_create

```odin
automation_recorder_create :: proc(settings: Automation_Recorder_Settings, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (node: core.Node, r: ^Automation_Recorder, err: core.Error)
```

Control thread. Makes a recorder node with no audio channels. Event-connect
it to the node whose parameters it writes.

### automation_recorder_arm

```odin
automation_recorder_arm :: proc(r: ^Automation_Recorder, armed: bool) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Arms or disarms writing, from the next block. Values are
passed on to the node either way.

### automation_recorder_set_punch

```odin
automation_recorder_set_punch :: proc(r: ^Automation_Recorder, punch_in: timebase.Beats, punch_out: timebase.Beats) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Writes only from timeline position `punch_in` to `punch_out`.

### automation_recorder_clear_punch

```odin
automation_recorder_clear_punch :: proc(r: ^Automation_Recorder) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Removes the punch range.

### automation_recorder_touch

```odin
automation_recorder_touch :: proc(r: ^Automation_Recorder, param: core.Param_Id, value: f64) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. The user takes hold of `param`'s control, at `value`:
writing starts. Suspend the parameter's automation player lane first
(`clip.automation_player_suspend`), so the two don't fight.

### automation_recorder_set

```odin
automation_recorder_set :: proc(r: ^Automation_Recorder, param: core.Param_Id, value: f64) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. The control moved: the node gets `value`, and it is
recorded if the parameter is being written.

### automation_recorder_release

```odin
automation_recorder_release :: proc(r: ^Automation_Recorder, param: core.Param_Id) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. The user lets go of `param`'s control. In `.Touch` mode
writing stops; in `.Latch` it goes on until the take ends.

### automation_recorder_poll

```odin
automation_recorder_poll :: proc(r: ^Automation_Recorder) -> (take: Automation_Take, ok: bool)
```

Control thread. The next finished range, if any (iterate with `for take
in`). The caller owns `take.points`.

### automation_recorder_dropped

```odin
automation_recorder_dropped :: proc "contextless"(r: ^Automation_Recorder) -> u64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Changes lost for lack of room (poll more often, or raise `max_events`).

### latency_probe_create

```odin
latency_probe_create :: proc(settings: Latency_Probe_Settings, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (node: core.Node, p: ^Latency_Probe, err: core.Error)
```

Control thread. Makes a probe node with one input and one output.

### latency_probe_start

```odin
latency_probe_start :: proc(p: ^Latency_Probe)
```

Control thread. Starts a measurement at the next block (the probe must
be in a running graph). It takes `max_seconds` plus the burst.

### latency_probe_result

```odin
latency_probe_result :: proc(p: ^Latency_Probe) -> (frames: int, quality: f64, ok: bool)
```

Control thread. The measured round trip in frames, once the measurement
is done (`ok`). `quality` is how cleanly the burst came back: the
normalised correlation, 1 for a perfect copy at any level; below about
0.5, the result is likely wrong (too quiet, or too noisy).

### midi_recorder_create

```odin
midi_recorder_create :: proc(settings: Midi_Recorder_Settings, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (node: core.Node, r: ^Midi_Recorder, err: core.Error)
```

Control thread. Makes a recorder node with no audio channels: connect
events into it (`graph.connect_events(g, graph.INPUT, id)` for the
device's MIDI input).

### midi_recorder_arm

```odin
midi_recorder_arm :: proc(r: ^Midi_Recorder, armed: bool) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Arms or disarms the recorder, from its next block. Armed,
it records while its timeline plays (and inside the punch range, if set).

### midi_recorder_set_latency

```odin
midi_recorder_set_latency :: proc(r: ^Midi_Recorder, frames: int) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Changes `latency_frames`, from the next block. Not while
recording.

### midi_recorder_set_punch

```odin
midi_recorder_set_punch :: proc(r: ^Midi_Recorder, punch_in: timebase.Beats, punch_out: timebase.Beats) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Records only from timeline position `punch_in` to `punch_out`.

### midi_recorder_clear_punch

```odin
midi_recorder_clear_punch :: proc(r: ^Midi_Recorder) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Removes the punch range.

### midi_recorder_poll

```odin
midi_recorder_poll :: proc(r: ^Midi_Recorder) -> (take: Midi_Take, ok: bool)
```

Control thread. Turns recorded events into clips, then returns the next
finished take, if any (iterate with `for take in`). The caller owns its
clip. A loop pass is finished when the timeline wraps.

### midi_recorder_progress

```odin
midi_recorder_progress :: proc(r: ^Midi_Recorder) -> (take: Midi_Take, ok: bool)
```

Control thread. The take being recorded, so far: its finished notes and
controllers (notes still held are left out until released). `ok` is false
when nothing is being recorded, or nothing changed since the last call;
otherwise the caller owns the clip. For overdubbing, merge it into the
clip that is playing as you go (see `clip.add_clip`).

### midi_recorder_status

```odin
midi_recorder_status :: proc "contextless"(r: ^Midi_Recorder) -> (recording: bool, dropped_events: u64)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Whether a take is being recorded, and the events lost so far for lack
of room (poll more often, or raise `max_events`).

### disk_writer_create

```odin
disk_writer_create :: proc(settings: Disk_Writer_Settings, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (d: ^Disk_Writer, err: core.Error)
```

Control thread. Starts the disk thread (unless `manual`). Free with
`disk_writer_destroy`, after the recorders using it.

### disk_writer_destroy

```odin
disk_writer_destroy :: proc(d: ^Disk_Writer)
```

Control thread. Stops the disk thread. Recorders still registered stop
being served.

### disk_writer_service

```odin
disk_writer_service :: proc(d: ^Disk_Writer) -> bool
```

Writes everything the recorders have queued. Returns whether there was
anything to do. The disk thread calls it; in `manual` mode, the app does
(any thread but the audio thread).

### register_types

```odin
register_types :: proc(reg: ^core.Node_Registry, disk: ^Disk_Writer = nil) -> core.Error
```

Registers this package's nodes. Audio recorders are registered only with
a `disk` to write through (it must outlive the registry). Control thread.
